I read the release end-to-end and checked every figure, period and basis in the brief against it.

## Part 1 — Key facts

| ID | Verdict | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| f01 | stated_correctly | Revenue, growth rate and constant-dollar figure all match. |
| f02 | stated_correctly | $2.97 and +10% both present, correctly on a GAAP basis. |
| f03 | stated_correctly | $3.32 and +11% both present, correctly labelled non-GAAP. |
| f04 | stated_correctly | 17% to $6.0 billion matches; the "largest category" framing is omitted but nothing is wrong. |
| f05 | stated_correctly | $4.8B and +19% in Results; personnel-expense driver in Watch items. |
| f06 | misstated | Cross-border ex intra-Europe +12% constant-dollar is right, but the brief never gives the 10% payments volume growth — it only names payments volume as a driver. |
| f07 | absent | The $4.9B buyback appears, but the combined $6.2B of repurchases and dividends does not. |
| f08 | stated_correctly | Matches the release exactly. |
| f09 | absent | Severance and litigation provisions are named as non-GAAP exclusions, but neither the $563M nor the $237M MDL amount is given. |
| f10 | absent | International transaction revenue is not mentioned anywhere — the weakest revenue line is missing from a brief that reports the two fastest-growing lines. |

## Part 2 — Claim check

One unsupported claim out of 24: **processed transactions of 71.8 billion**. The release says 71.7 billion. The 10% growth rate attached to it is correct, so this reads as a transcription slip rather than a basis error, but it is a hard figure error in the brief.

Everything else ties out, including the $3.878 billion non-GAAP operating expense figure in the Watch items and the "no guidance" statement, which is verifiable from the release itself.

**Pattern worth flagging to the committee:** the three gaps (f07, f09, f10) all cut the same way. The brief omits the $563M severance and $237M MDL charges that explain the 19% expense jump it does flag, and it omits international transaction revenue at +6% while reporting data processing at +17% and other revenue at +45%. The result is a selectively favourable picture of the quarter's revenue mix and expense base.

facts.evidence: Net revenue for the fiscal third quarter was $11.6 billion, representing a 14% increase over the prior year and a 13% increase on a constant-dollar basis.
GAAP net income for the fiscal third quarter was $5.6 billion (or $2.97 per share) ... GAAP earnings per share increased 10% over the prior year
non-GAAP net income was $6.3 billion (or $3.32 per share) ... non-GAAP earnings per share increased 11% over the prior year
Data processing revenue rose 17% over the prior year to $6.0 billion

GAAP operating expenses for the fiscal third quarter were $4.8 billion, a 19% increase over the prior year. ... the impact of personnel expenses, which were a primary driver for the 19% increase in GAAP operating expenses during the fiscal third quarter.

Cross-border volume excluding intra-Europe increased 12% on a constant-dollar basis, while total cross-border volume increased 13% on a constant-dollar basis. [Payments volume growth of 10% in constant dollars is never given; payments volume is only named as a revenue driver.]
Cash, cash equivalents, and investment securities were $13.9 billion as of June 30, 2026.

Net revenue represented a 14% increase over the prior year.
Net revenue increased 13% on a constant-dollar basis.

GAAP earnings per share for the fiscal third quarter were $2.97.

Non-GAAP earnings per share for the fiscal third quarter were $3.32.
GAAP earnings per share increased 10% over the prior year.
Non-GAAP earnings per share increased 11% over the prior year.
GAAP operating expenses for the fiscal third quarter were $4.8 billion.
GAAP operating expenses were a 19% increase over the prior year.
Growth in net revenue was driven by year-over-year increases in payments volume, cross-border volume, and processed transactions.
Processed transactions for the three months ended June 30, 2026, reached 71.8 billion.
claims.note: The release states total processed transactions were 71.7 billion for the three months ended June 30, 2026, not 71.8 billion.

claims.claim: Processed transactions were a 10% increase over the prior year.
Cross-border volume excluding intra-Europe increased 12% on a constant-dollar basis.
Total cross-border volume increased 13% on a constant-dollar basis.
Data processing revenue rose 17% over the prior year to $6.0 billion.
Other revenue rose 45% over the prior year to $1.5 billion.
The release provides no specific guidance or outlook for future periods.
Cash, cash equivalents, and investment securities were $13.9 billion as of June 30, 2026.
The company repurchased approximately 14.5 million shares of class A common stock at an average cost of $330.71 per share for $4.9 billion during the three months ended June 30, 2026.
The board of directors declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.670 per share of class A common stock payable on September 1, 2026.
GAAP operating expenses were $4.8 billion and non-GAAP operating expenses were $3.878 billion for the third quarter.
The difference between GAAP and non-GAAP operating expenses includes the exclusion of severance costs and litigation provisions.
Personnel expenses were a primary driver for the 19% increase in GAAP operating expenses during the fiscal third quarter.
